toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate of 0.41% is inside the service's normal range. Over the previous 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher, and each investigation found no fault. The burn-rate page did not fire, because the burn was 0.82x against a threshold of 2x. Request counts are stable, and the dashboard query is unchanged and matches a recount of the raw logs. Customer bookings and complaints show no effect.

The new-pod versus old-pod comparison during the v4.18 rollout is not evidence against the release. Every recent rollout shows the same gap, including a config-only redeploy of the unchanged v4.16 image. Freshly started pods have cold caches and produce a few timeouts. That adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, far too few to explain the weekly rise.

Recommendation: don't roll back. Record the week as normal and run the standard check on the following week. Keep all alerting on; muting it would remove the only protection. I'm fairly confident in this. I did not establish a cause for the small rise, because the replica move and partner-sync traffic remain untested. Look at those only if next week also exceeds the band.
